subject: Mutual Action Plan & contract gating — Cornell BioSystems evaluation
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Ward <ethan.ward@cornellbio.com>, Maria Santos <maria.santos@cornellbio.com>, procurement@cornellbio.com
Cc: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan & contract gating — Cornell BioSystems evaluation

Hi Ethan / Maria / procurement team,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the run-through of the evaluation priorities. Per our conversation, attaching a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a draft SOW so your team can see how we’re proposing the evaluation -> pilot -> production sequence. High-level ask: can you confirm the procurement & legal owners and any hard gating dates we should be aware of?

Quick summary of the gating/dependency items in the MAP:
- Contract stack: MSA (base legal terms) -> DPA (data handling + residency) -> Order Form (pricing and term) — order form is sequenced to sign after DPA redline acceptance
- Security evidence required before pilot: SOC 2 summary (attached), data flow diagram, and encryption/KMS confirmation
- Acceptance criteria for pilot: throughput/latency targets, sample prompts, and a short eval report (we’ll provide a template)
- Target timeline (provisional): legal review week of Aug 24, procurement approvals by Sep 3, pilot start Sep 10, production cutover Oct 1

Attachments (stubs): 20260817_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with milestone dates), Cornell_SOW_draft_v2.docx, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Next steps I recommend:
1) Please confirm the legal owner and procurement approver (name + email)
2) If there are DPA redlines your legal team needs upfront, send them to me and I’ll route to our privacy counsel; flag any high-priority clauses (data residency, subprocessors, deletion windows)
3) Marcus/Dev — can you confirm whether we can accept the DPA deletion window of 30 days (we typically support 30–45 days) and whether the SOW needs a data residency addendum?

Goal is to lock the MAP and contract sequencing this week so procurement has clear milestones.

Thanks,
--
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

From: Ethan Ward <ethan.ward@cornellbio.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Maria Santos <maria.santos@cornellbio.com>
Cc: procurement@cornellbio.com, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & contract gating — Cornell BioSystems evaluation

Naomi — thanks for pulling this together and for the attachments. Quick responses from our side:

- Procurement owner is Maria Santos (cc’d). Legal review will be handled by our counsel; target to complete first pass by Aug 24, but that depends on how many DPA redlines we raise.
- We do need the DPA and SOW to include a simple data flow diagram that shows: where data is sent, what is stored, and which tenants (if any) are co-located. Can you add that to the SOW?
- SOC2 summary looks good as an initial artifact; our security team will request the full bridge letter if needed but won’t block the pilot on that alone.

Procurement note: our finance team prefers Order Form signature only after DPA and MSA are agreed and procurement coding is set. If you can sequence the order form for signature after legal acceptance, that would be ideal.

I’ll push to get legal comments to you by Aug 24. If that slips, we’ll update the MAP.

Thanks — Ethan
Ethan Ward
Head of AI Platforms | Cornell BioSystems
ethan.ward@cornellbio.com | +1 617-555-0199

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & contract gating — Cornell BioSystems evaluation

Thanks — quick alignment from legal/solutions on sequencing and what we can commit to:

Summary of sequence we propose (short, actionable):
- Step 1: MSA base terms (Redwood standard) — target first-pass redlines returned by Cornell legal by 2026-08-24
- Step 2: DPA negotiation in parallel with MSA; Redwood can accept a 30-day deletion window and the standard subprocessor disclosure process. Any data residency addendum will be handled via an appendix in the SOW if required.
- Step 3: Order Form prepared with pricing and SKU details — sign after MSA+DPA are agreed and procurement coding is complete (Redwood ok with signing Order Form with a mutually agreed effective date)

Pilot acceptance criteria (to attach to Order Form/SOW):
- Latency: 95th percentile < 450ms for 1k token prompt set
- Throughput: sustained 20 requests/sec baseline for evaluation window
- Quality check: pass 3 of 4 evaluation prompt categories (safety, correctness, hallucination tolerance, throughput)

Open items for Cornell to confirm by Aug 24:
- Legal contact for redlines (who will send first pass)
- Procurement approver and PO timeline
- Any export control / data residency hard constraints that would change the SOW

If Cornell can confirm those by Aug 24 we’ll lock the MAP milestones and I’ll circulate an updated MAP with final dates. Naomi — I’m happy to host a short call with Cornell legal if they want to walk the DPA clauses line-by-line.

Thanks,
--
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
